title: Write independent review 2 of the revised study capability M1 design
summary: I read 'the revised study design' as docs/design/study-capability-m1.md, which was revised after review 1 and says it needs a re-check before building. The job writes an independent review 2 in docs/design/reviews/. It checks the review-1 dispositions and the revision for new defects against the §9 checks. It does not edit the design.

defaults_applied.how: The request names no file. The repository shows one design that asks for a re-check, so I read it that way and did not ask.
Every finding in the review must cite a section or a BRIEF.md line, and counts are marked as counted or estimated.
The review is written to stand alone, in the format of review 1.
One new review file; the design itself is not edited.
The review's own citations and anchors are checked against the tree, and cargo test must still pass.
Re-checking is the §9 review gate for a significant design before it is built.

assumptions: 'The revised study design' is docs/design/study-capability-m1.md, which its own header says was revised after review 1 and needs a re-check (review 2) before building.
'Re-check' means write an independent review 2 in docs/design/reviews/, not edit the design. Findings are reported to the user; the design is left for its author to answer.
No model call or run of a studied system is needed; the review is by reading and by checks that only read the repository, as in review 1.
The review does not pass or fail the design for the user; it gives a verdict and lists decisions for the user.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new file docs/design/reviews/study-capability-m1-review-2.md exists, in the format of review 1: verdict, severity scale, stable finding ids, a section per check, decisions for the user, and an appendix of experiments.
The review follows the eight checks of §9 of docs/design/study-capability-m1.md and records a result (pass or findings) for each.
The review verifies each of the 15 dispositions and the 8 decisions in Appendix A against the revised design text, citing section and line, and says where a claimed fix is absent or only partial.

The review checks the revision for new defects. Candidates: the 'Quote mismatch' rule is classed as evidence but Appendix A names only 'six' evidence rules; the rule counts and classes are inconsistent; §5.4 'Unsupported number' cannot test a missing label if the type refuses it; whether §2.1 containment and the provider-side spend limit are feasible; and whether the A4-A 'chosen for review' wording is stale.
Each BRIEF.md line number cited in the review matches BRIEF.md in the tree, and each in-document anchor the review relies on resolves.
The review makes no claim about firstmate and states its verdict (approve, approve with changes, or return) and the consequence under §9 for scheduling a build.
The review file is the only reviewed document changed: docs/design/study-capability-m1.md is not edited by this job, and the existing review-1 file is unchanged.
Run `git status` and `git diff --stat`: only the new review file (and optionally a CHANGELOG.md entry) appears. Run `cargo test` and confirm it passes, including the xtask policy tests.

out_of_scope: Creating the athena-cap-study crate or any Rust code
Changing governance files such as athena.toml, defaults.toml, CI workflows, or Cargo.toml lints
departures: Small upward shift in cost: the review must read a long design (about 490 lines), BRIEF.md and review 1, then write a long document. P(reading accepted) is a little lower than the reference because 're-check' could also mean edit the design.
